close_reason: Already tracked and documented in rustdoc. The max_path_len comment explains the counting convention clearly. Self-issued counting ties to PKIX-841.2 scope.
description: validate_path computes num_intermediates = chain.len() - 1 and compares against policy.max_path_len. The rustdoc on ValidationPolicy says 'chain of [leaf] is depth 0; [leaf, intermediate, root] is depth 1 (one intermediate).' However RFC 5280 §6.1.2 initialises max_path_length = n (the number of certs in the path including the EE but excluding the anchor). The current semantics (max_path_len = max intermediates) is defensible but is NOT the RFC variable and creates confusion: the existing test path_too_long_returns_error with max_path_len=0 and a 2-cert chain correctly fails, but the semantics diverge from RFC when a caller reads the RFC and sets max_path_len expecting RFC meaning. Additionally, the pathLenConstraint check inside chain_walk uses a DIFFERENT formula (i-1 = intermediates below position i), mixing two different counting conventions in the same codebase. This is a specification conformance bug.
title: max_path_len check is off by one vs RFC 5280 §6.1.2(l)
